title: Forget the next 3 weeks; think about the next 3 years. 5 large-cap stocks with upside potential of up to 31%
summary: The markets are up one day and down the next, and the bears are all around. How to deal with such volatility? Well, you could watch from the sidelines and wait for things to improve. The problem, however, is that, by the time you figure out things have improved, stock prices would have moved up. So, use the opportunity to look at the underlying business and management of companies you are interested in. If the numbers are good and management has a track record of delivering, ignore everything else. But with some caveats.

title: The bond rout is bruising would-be home buyers—and challenging the Fed
summary: Investors’ worries about government debt, plus their increased expectations that the Fed will hike rates this year, are also affecting bond prices and raising yields.

title: Expert view: Semiconductors, spacetech could unlock $500 bn-$1 tn market opportunity, says Piper Serica's Director
summary: India appears to be on the brink of a technology revolution, with semiconductors, spacetech, and deeptech poised to reshape its economic landscape. Ajay Modi, Director at Piper Serica, believes these industries have the potential to create a market opportunity of $500 billion to $1 trillion.&nbsp;

title: ETF market price vs NAV: Why some funds trade at a 20% premium while others stay close to fair value?
summary: Most domestic ETFs are trading close to their NAV, while some international ETFs trade at steep premiums due to supply constraints. Experts advise investors to compare an ETF's market price with its NAV or iNAV to avoid overpaying and make better investment decisions.

title: Credit cards: A financial convenience or a debt trap? Experts explain how smart usage makes the difference
summary: Credit cards offer convenience, rewards and credit-building opportunities, but only when used responsibly. Experts explain how timely repayments and disciplined spending can help individuals avoid debt, improve credit scores and maximise financial benefits while reducing borrowing risks.

title: US market at record highs, China still cheap: Where should Indian investors invest?
summary: Indian investors are reevaluating portfolio strategies amid market volatility. The US offers growth but is expensive, whereas China is cheaper yet carries risks. Experts suggest global diversification, with a recommended allocation of 15-25% for beginners and up to 50% for aggressive profiles.
